title: Raft consensus
description: How Raft keeps a replicated log consistent: elections, replication, safety. Notes from the paper and the TLA+ spec.

intents.title: Randomized election timeouts
intents.body: Each follower waits a random 150–300 ms before standing as a candidate, so split votes are rare and resolve quickly. Tuned against the [[AppendEntries doubles as the heartbeat|heartbeat]] interval. #liveness

intents.title: Terms are logical clocks
intents.body: Every message carries the sender's term. A server that sees a higher term steps down to follower and adopts it; stale leaders discover they are stale on their next RPC. #safety

intents.title: What happens on a split vote in a four-node cluster?
AppendEntries doubles as the heartbeat
intents.body: Empty AppendEntries keep followers from timing out; the same RPC carries new entries plus the index and term of the entry before them. #liveness

intents.title: Log matching property
intents.body: If two logs contain an entry with the same index and term, the logs are identical up to that index. The consistency check in AppendEntries maintains it inductively.

intents.title: Commit = replicated on a majority in the current term
intents.body: A leader only counts replicas for entries from its own term; older entries commit indirectly. This is what [[Leader completeness]] relies on. #safety

intents.title: Leader completeness
intents.body: Voters refuse candidates whose log is less up-to-date (compare last term, then length), so any elected leader holds every committed entry. Enforced by the [[Up-to-date check]]. #safety

intents.title: Why can't a leader commit an old-term entry by counting replicas? (Figure 8)
In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm
intents.body: Ongaro & Ousterhout, 2014. Sections 5.2–5.4 cover election, replication and safety.
